description: The Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia, in Formal Case No. 1149, by Order No. 23131, dated July 29, 2026, among other things, approved a two-year pilot extending Senior Citizen and Disabled Residents Rate Credit for the period of October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2028.

PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION OF THE DISTRICT OF COLUMBIA 
1325 G STREET, N.W., SUITE 800 
WASHINGTON, D.C. 20005

FORMAL CASE NO. 1149, IN THE MATTER OF THE INVESTIGATION INTO THE 
STRUCTURE AND APPLICATION OF AN EXPERIMENTAL RATE CLASS FOR 
BOTH SENIOR CITIZENS AND DISABLED RESIDENTS IN THE DISTRICT OF 
COLUMBIA, Order No. 23131 
I.
INTRODUCTION
1.
By this Order, the Public Service Commission of the District of Columbia
(“Commission”) hereby approves a two-year pilot extending Senior Citizen and Disabled 
Residents Rate Credit (“Rider SCADRRC” or “Program”) for the period of October 1, 2026, 
through September 30, 2028, in accordance with Paragraphs 14-19 of this Order. In accordance 
with Paragraphs 20-29 herein, the Commission also directs the Potomac Electric Power Company 
(“Pepco” or “Company”) to: (1) conduct market research and additional analysis; (2) convene 
stakeholder meetings; (3) assume responsibility for the annual eligibility-identification process; 
(4) submit annual program statistics; and (5) file a Final Program Evaluation Report by
March 31, 2028. Non-stakeholder participants may file comments on the Final Program
Evaluation Report within thirty (30) days.
II.
BACKGROUND
2.
On July 25, 2017, the Commission issued Order No. 18846 announcing its intention
to “open a new proceeding to discuss the parameters around creating a new experimental rate class 
for both senior citizens and disabled residents within the District.”1 The Order also adopted the 
Pepco recommendation that the Commission open a separate docket to explore bill affordability 
for customers who do not qualify for the Residential Aid Discount (“RAD”), such as working 
families and retirees.2 The Commission stated that the parameters around creating this 
experimental rate class should be examined through technical conferences and that the eventual 
discount rate would target District of Columbia (“District”) residents who need rate assistance but 
have not received it. The Commission also stated that eligibility should be as simple, trouble-free,

3. 
On October 19, 2017, the Commission issued Order No. 19146, opening Formal 
Case No. 1149 to “investigate the structure and application of an experimental rate class for both 
senior citizens and disabled residents in the District,” and scheduling the first technical conference 
regarding the experimental rate class for December 19, 2017.5 Three technical conferences were 
convened in this matter between December 19, 2017, and March 19, 2018. On April 9, 2018, 
pursuant to Commission Order No. 19146, Commission Staff, on behalf of the technical 
conference participants, submitted the Final Report.6 On November 18, 2018, the Commission 
accepted the Final Report as filed and recognized the need for designing a new electricity discount 
program for senior citizens and disabled residents in the District.7 The Commission accepted the 
Final Report’s recommendation that the experimental senior and disabled discount be a fixed 
monthly credit. The Commission required that the credit equal $7.50 a month for qualified 
customers, finding this amount to be reasonable.8 The Commission also directed Pepco to file a 
notice when only 24 months of funding remained from the $6 million in Pepco-Exelon Merger-
provided Consumer Rate Base Credits (“CRBC”) allocated to support the experimental senior 
citizen and disabled rate credit.9 

4. 
On August 1, 2025, Pepco notified the Commission that the funds supporting Rider 
SCADRRC are expected to be exhausted by September 30, 2025, effectively ending the credit on 
October 1, 2025.10 As such, Pepco claims that the $7.50 monthly credit will no longer appear on 
eligible customer bills after that date.11 In addition, Rider SCADRRC will also be removed from 
the tariff. Pepco states that a residual balance is expected to remain after the program ends, which 
will be incorporated into the 2025 Annual Bill Stabilization Adjustment Reconciliation for the 
residential rate class.12 However, Pepco states that it is open to considering other funding sources

5.

7. 
On October 1, 2025, the Commission issued Order No. 22719 authorizing a one-
year regulatory asset, capped at $1.5 million, to continue Rider SCADRRC from October 1, 2025, 
through September 30, 2026, while the Commission evaluated longer-term options.25 Order 
No. 22719 also directed Commission Staff to convene a technical conference and required a final 
report addressing: (1) the Program’s impact, including a detailed annual cost-benefit analysis; (2) 
alternative funding mechanisms; (3) alternative methods for identifying and qualifying customers; 
(4) at least three years of projected continuation costs; and (5) recommendations, including 
projected bill impacts, concerning the allocation of future Program costs and the regulatory asset.26 

8. 
Commission Staff convened technical conferences on November 12, 2025, 
January 15, 2026, and February 20, 2026. Participants included the OPC, AOBA, NCLC, the 
Department of Energy and Environment (“DOEE”), AARP DC, Commission Staff, and Pepco 
(collectively, “Stakeholders”). Pepco filed the Technical Conference Final Report on March 27, 
2026.27 

III. 
SUMMARY OF FINAL TECHNICAL CONFERENCE REPORT 

9. 
The Final Technical Conference Report (“Final TC Report”) described the host of 
topics related to the Rider SCADRRC discussed across the three meetings, including, but not 
limited to: program enrollment, administration, customer usage, arrearages and disconnections, 
geographic correlations with socioeconomic indicators, projected Program costs, and potential rate 
impacts. The Report also includes an appendix of additional comments and position statements 
from each Stakeholder. 

10. 
Pepco reported that Program enrollment declined from 16,046 participants in 2020 
to 14,903 participants in 2025. Pepco also explained that approximately ten percent of accounts 
require annual manual review and estimated that, if the current eligibility and enrollment criteria 
remain unchanged, the Program would cost approximately $1.4 million to $1.5 million per year,28 
with a projected $0.35 average annual bill impact for residential customers over a 3-year period.29

Pepco further reported that Rider SCADRRC customers had a lower arrearage percentage than the 
overall customer pool.30 

11. 
The Final TC Report also identified material limits in the existing record. Pepco 
stated that it lacks the participant-level demographic data and an approved cost-benefit 
methodology needed to measure the precise impact of the monthly credit.31 DOEE compared 
Program enrollment by ZIP code with socioeconomic indicators and found positive correlations 
with food-assistance participation and negative correlations with higher household income and 
bachelor’s-degree attainment. DOEE explained, however, that the geographic analysis was 
suggestive rather than direct proof of participant need or Program effects. DOEE therefore 
recommended a more robust evaluation, including customer research designed to examine 
participant characteristics, awareness, experiences, and preferences.32 

12. 
The Stakeholders did not reach a common position on whether the Rider should be 
continued, how the program should be designed, or how the Rider should be funded/recovered. 
Their positions are summarized as follows: 

(a) AARP DC supports continued assistance and favors a means-tested program targeted 
to customers in need. AARP DC stated that General Fund or other taxpayer funding 
would be preferable. If the Program is to be funded through utility rates, AARP DC 
favors a cap, disclosure of nonparticipant impacts, and allocation across all ratepayers.33 
(b) AOBA opposes continuation of the Rider and an additional regulatory asset absent 
empirical evidence establishing need. AOBA emphasized cost-shifting and cumulative 
rate-burden concerns and stated that, at a minimum, the Commission should adopt 
appropriate income and participation criteria if the Program continues.34 
(c) DOEE supports continuation of the Rider on an extended-pilot basis. DOEE views its 
geographic analysis as suggestive evidence that the Program reaches households likely 
to need assistance, characterized the projected bill impact as low if costs were spread 
across all ratepayers, and recommended a more holistic evaluation. DOEE also offered 
to assist Pepco with evaluation design and recommends considering whether the same 
funding could have greater impact through other assistance programs.35

(d) NCLC supports continuing the Rider using the current eligibility criteria and favored 
spreading costs among ratepayers. NCLC characterized the Program as simple to 
administer and modest in cost stating that enrollment of otherwise eligible customers in 
RAD could be an acceptable alternative to continuing the Rider.36 
(e) OPC supports an extended pilot to permit additional review and recommendations. 
OPC urged the Commission to examine funding sources, impacts on participating and 
paying customers, energy justice, environmental justice, and alternative methods of 
assisting eligible customers. OPC also cautioned that the available arrearage data could 
indicate that the most financially vulnerable customers are not the principal 
beneficiaries of the existing credit.37 
(f) PEPCO takes no position on continuation or future funding. Pepco estimated that costs 
would remain between approximately $1.4 million and $1.5 million per year under the 
existing criteria, acknowledged limitations in its ability to assess customer impacts, and 
stated that it was open to further Commission direction.38 
13. 
The Final TC Report concluded that the Stakeholders had not reached consensus 
on whether Rider SCADRRC should continue or how future costs should be funded and 
allocated.39 

IV. 
DECISION 

14. 
The Commission appreciates the work undertaken by the Stakeholders to consider 
the implications of continuing the Rider SCADRRC. While Stakeholders did not reach a 
consensus recommendation, we find merit in various aspects of the recommendations provided 
and for the reasons discussed below, will continue the Rider SCADRRC as a two-year pilot from 
October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2028. The pilot will maintain the current fixed monthly 
credit of $7.50 and the existing eligibility criteria. The Commission also authorizes Pepco to 
continue the existing regulatory asset or establish a new regulatory asset to record the incremental 
credit amounts provided during the pilot, subject to a total cap of $3 million and later review in a 
Pepco base rate case. 

15. 
As described in greater detail below, to develop a more complete record before 
deciding whether the Rider SCADRRC should continue beyond the two-year pilot, the 
Commission directs Pepco to: (1) conduct market research and additional analysis; (2) convene 
stakeholder meetings; (3) assume responsibility for the annual eligibility-identification process; 
(4) submit annual program statistics; and (5) file a Final Program Evaluation Report by 
March 31, 2028.

A. 
Two-Year Pilot 

16. 
The present record supports continuation of Rider SCADRRC, but it does not yet 
support a final determination regarding the Program’s structure, funding, or permanent 
continuation. AARP DC and NCLC support continued assistance, while DOEE and OPC support 
an extended pilot. DOEE’s analysis provides suggestive evidence that the Program reaches 
communities likely in need of assistance. At the same time, Pepco and DOEE identify important 
data limitations, OPC calls for a broader fairness and impact analysis, and AOBA raises concerns 
regarding demonstrated need, cost shifting, and cumulative rate impacts. These competing 
considerations favor continuation of a defined pilot with a cost cap, and an opportunity to collect 
additional data related to the program’s benefits and consumer impacts. This two-year pilot 
extension preserves continuity for current participants while permitting the Commission to obtain 
information that the technical conference record does not presently contain. 

17. 
The period from October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2028, also provides 
sufficient time to develop and approve an evaluation plan, conduct market research, collect 
additional Program data, present resulting information to Stakeholders, and develop a final 
recommendation before the pilot expires. 

18. 
During the pilot, the monthly credit will remain $7.50 and the existing eligibility 
criteria will remain in effect; reducing the risk of changes in enrollment or projected Program cost 
caused by mid-pilot eligibility modifications. Pepco shall continue to work to administer the credit 
so that existing eligible participants experience no lapse in receipt of the credit. 

19. 
To fund the credits during the pilot, Pepco may, at its election, continue the 
regulatory asset authorized by Order No. 22719 or establish a new regulatory asset of the same 
type. The additional principal recorded for credits provided from October 1, 2026, through 
September 30, 2028, shall not exceed $3 million.40 Pepco shall separately track amounts 
associated with the prior one-year extension and the two-year pilot. Recovery, prudence, and 
allocation of the regulatory asset will be reviewed in a Pepco base rate case. This accounting 
authorization does not pre-determine the amount or allocation of any future recovery. 

B. 
Program Administration and Annual Reporting 

20. 
Beginning October 1, 2026, Pepco shall assume responsibility for the annual 
process of identifying customers who meet the existing Rider SCADRRC eligibility criteria and 
for creating and maintaining the annual Program eligibility database. For the first cycle, Pepco 
shall perform the work occurring from October through December 2026 that is necessary to 
establish the database for the eligibility cycle beginning in January 2027. Commission Staff shall 
coordinate with Pepco and provide transition assistance. Pepco will remain responsible for 
completing the process on schedule and for preventing any interruption in credits to existing 
eligible participants. 

40 
Pepco shall also notify the Commission within five (5) months of expending the Program funds or reaching 
the $3 million Program cap. 

Order No. 23131 Page No. 8 

21. 
Pepco shall also file annual Program statistics until directed otherwise. The first 
annual report shall be filed no later than March 1, 2027, shall cover calendar year 2026, and shall 
describe the October-December 2026 transition and the status of the January 2027 eligibility 
database. Each annual report shall be filed by March 1 and include, at a minimum: (1) enrollment; 
(2) the number and aggregate number of credits provided; (3) total Program costs; (4) participant 
electricity usage (average monthly, median, and quartile data); (5) participant electric bill 
arrearages; and (6) disconnections. 

C. 
Evaluation Plan and Stakeholder Engagement 

22. 
As summarized above, in the Final TC Report, DOEE specifically recommended 
direct customer research and offered to assist with a more robust evaluation, while OPC and AOBA 
emphasized the need for stronger evidence regarding need, impact, fairness, and alternatives. The 
data and research requirements directed below are designed to address the concerns raised by 
stakeholders in the Final TC Report and to develop a record responsive to the Stakeholders’ 
competing concerns to inform the Commission’s final determination on program continuance after 
the two-year pilot. 

23. 
No later than October 15, 2026, Pepco shall file a Draft Program Evaluation Plan 
consisting of a draft outline for the March 2028 Final Program Evaluation Report and an 
accompanying market-research plan. The Draft Program Evaluation Plan shall contain: (1) a list 
of Program data to be gathered and included in the Final Program Evaluation Report, informed by 
prior Stakeholder recommendations, with the expected source of each data element; (2) a market-
research plan designed to examine participant characteristics and preferences, including a research 
schedule, the proposed use of a participant survey and/or focus group(s), a draft survey instrument 
and/or focus-group guide, and a research budget; and (3) an outline of the Final Program 
Evaluation Report’s findings and recommendations section addressing Program continuation, 
improvements, administration, future cost estimates, future Program cost recovery, and alternative 
programs and/or methods of assisting ratepayers. 

24. 
Pepco shall convene a Stakeholder working group meeting no later than 
November 1, 2026, to discuss the Draft Program Evaluation Plan and obtain Stakeholder feedback. 
Pepco shall file meeting minutes within ten (10) days of the working group meeting. 

25. 
No later than November 15, 2026, Pepco shall file a revised Final Program 
Evaluation Plan for Commission review and approval. The filing shall reflect and address 
Stakeholder feedback received at the first working group meeting. Pepco may consult with DOEE 
and other Stakeholders in developing and carrying out the evaluation plan, but Pepco shall remain 
responsible for all deliverables, meetings, filings, schedules, and budgets required by this Order. 

26. 
Pepco shall convene a technical conference no later than November 1, 2027, or 
earlier if the approved Final Program Evaluation Plan work is complete, to present the market-
research results, Program data collected, and analyses performed. Pepco shall also obtain 
Stakeholder feedback, questions, and initial consensus and non-consensus positions on Program 
continuation. Pepco shall file meeting minutes within ten (10) days of the technical conference. 

Order No. 23131 Page No. 9 

27. 
Pepco shall convene a second working group meeting no later than 
January 30, 2028, to discuss the Program findings, address remaining Stakeholder questions and 
data requests from the technical conference, and finalize Stakeholder recommendations on 
Program continuation. Pepco shall file meeting minutes within ten (10) days of the second working 
group meeting. 

D. 
Final Report and Next Steps 

28. 
No later than March 31, 2028, on behalf of all Stakeholders, Pepco shall file a Final 
Program Evaluation Report. The report shall include: (1) the final Program data; (2) the market-
research methodology, instruments, results, and analysis; (3) an assessment of participant 
characteristics, awareness, experiences, and preferences; (4) an evaluation of Program 
administration, costs, usage, arrearages, disconnections, and observed benefits or limitations; (5) 
a summary of Stakeholder feedback received during the evaluation process; and (6) specific 
working group consensus and non-consensus recommendations concerning Program continuation 
or termination, Program improvements, Program administration, future cost estimates for at least 
three years, and future cost-recovery, including proposed class allocation and projected bill 
impacts. 

29. 
Non-stakeholder participants may file comments on the Final Program Evaluation 
Report within thirty (30) days. After reviewing the Final Program Evaluation Report and 
Stakeholder comments, the Commission will determine whether to continue the Rider SCADRRC 
beyond the two-year pilot period. 

THEREFORE, IT IS ORDERED THAT:

from October 1, 2026, through September 30, 2028, with a fixed monthly credit of $7.50 for
